{{short description|Austrian scientist}}
'''Stefanie Tschegg''' (born 7 July 1943 in [[Graz]]) is an emeritus at the [[University of Natural Resources and Life Sciences, Vienna]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.boku.ac.at/personen/person/162CD598D2AB57A6/|title=Stefanie Tschegg, Univ.-Prof. i.R. Dr.phil.::Personen::BOKU|website=www.boku.ac.at|access-date=2019-02-08}}</ref>

== Life ==
Tschegg received her doctoral degree from the University of Vienna in 1971.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://forschung.boku.ac.at/fis/suchen.person_uebersicht?sprache_in=en&menue_id_in=101&id_in=535|title=University of Natural Resources and Life Sciences, Vienna (BOKU) – Research portal|website=forschung.boku.ac.at|access-date=2019-02-08}}</ref> From 1980 to 1981, she was a visiting associate professor at [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]].<ref name=":0" /> She finished her habilitation in physics in 1982.<ref name=":0" /> In 1989, she became a professor of physics at the [[University of Natural Resources and Life Sciences, Vienna]].<ref name=":0" />

== Research ==
Some of her research interests are:

* Structure, mechanical and fracture mechanical properties of different materials<ref name=":0" />
* Development and application of material testing methods (especially methods based on [[wikt:ultrasonic|ultrasonic]])<ref name=":0" />

* 1977 Theodor Körner Award<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://cost-fp0802.tuwien.ac.at/organisation/management-committee/austria/stefanie-tschegg/curriculum-vitae.html|title=COST Action FP0802: Curriculum Vitae|website=cost-fp0802.tuwien.ac.at|language=en|access-date=2019-02-08}}</ref>
* 1983 Kardinal Innitzer Award<ref name=":1" />

* 2011 Honorary Member of German Association for Materials Science and Testing (DVM) <ref name=":0" />
